target_constraint: Must prevent bacterial contamination during and after surgery
mechanism: The evidence shows that intraocular inflammation can be triggered by non-infectious biological agents (e.g., inactivated vaccine) and that fungal endophthalmitis (e.g., Fusarium) can arise from anterior segment surgery, indicating that both sterile inflammation and fungal contamination are distinct pathways that can mimic or complicate bacterial infection. This suggests that a broad-spectrum antimicrobial surface that also mitigates sterile inflammation could reduce the risk of postoperative endophthalmitis beyond bacterial prophylaxis alone.
intervention: Coat the intraocular lens (IOL) optic and haptics with a dual-action polymer layer that (1) releases a sustained low-dose of a broad-spectrum antifungal and antibacterial agent (e.g., a combination of moxifloxacin and amphotericin B) over 7–14 days post-implantation, and (2) incorporates a corticosteroid-eluting component (e.g., dexamethasone) to suppress sterile inflammatory responses triggered by surgical trauma or foreign-body reaction, thereby preventing both bacterial and fungal colonization and reducing inflammation that can exacerbate infection.
expected_effect: The IOL would actively prevent bacterial and fungal adhesion and growth on its surface and in the capsular bag during the critical postoperative window, while simultaneously dampening inflammation, reducing the incidence of postoperative endophthalmitis (both bacterial and fungal) and associated complications like capsular bag distension syndrome.
falsification_test: In a rabbit model of cataract surgery, implant the coated IOL in one eye and a standard IOL with intracameral antibiotic injection in the contralateral eye. Inoculate both eyes with a subclinical dose of Staphylococcus epidermidis and Fusarium solani. At 7 days, culture aqueous and vitreous humor and assess clinical inflammation scores. If the coated IOL does not show significantly lower culture positivity and lower inflammation scores compared to the control, the intervention is falsified.
